name: Joan of Arc lifts siege of Orléans
summary: Joan of Arc, a 17-year-old peasant girl from Domrémy claiming divine visions, arrives at the besieged city of Orléans (April 29, 1429) with a relief army. Within nine days, the English siege works, besieging the city since October 1428, are destroyed. Joan leads the assault on the fortress of Les Tourelles personally; the English siege is broken (May 8, 1429). The relief of Orléans reverses the momentum of the Hundred Years' War; Charles VII is crowned at Reims in July 1429. Joan is captured (1430) and burned at Rouen by the English-sponsored court (May 30, 1431).

_quarry.structural_significance: Turns the tide of the Hundred Years' War decisively; enables Charles VII's coronation; creates the most powerful symbol of French nationalism; demonstrates the power of charismatic religious motivation in warfare
